caption: Simulation-time playback, seen from straight above: the 38,730-tetrahedron Baymax body, 135 mm across, lies on its back; a planar blade cuts the belly along the midline, 28.5 mm long and 13.5 mm deep where the body is 42 mm thick (not through: the Line tool of the window cuts through the whole depth of the view, this blade goes through the same cut call), and two right-drag grips, one on each side, are pulled 4 mm and 8 mm outward and stay as spring holds (green markers) that keep the wound about 8.5 mm open. The floor holds the body against the grips by friction (coefficient 0.5). The body rests on the floor: its lowest point is 0.3 mm under the floor's plane, and the belly top settles about 2 mm in the first 0.3 s as the soft body flattens on its round back. From 3.5 s to 6.5 s, while the second grip pulls the wound open, the viewer's Show Edges option is on: the dark lines are the edges of the triangles that the example draws, which are the surface of the simulated tetrahedral mesh itself, not a finer drawing mesh (9,882 faces of tetrahedra with a median edge of 1.9 mm before the cut, about 10,800 triangles after it; the 860 or so on the two walls of the wound and those at the body's outline are seen at a grazing angle and merge into dark hatching). The picture is the middle 800x660 of the 1280x720 recording: the side panel and the counters are cut off. Playback at 60 frames/s does not measure live FPS.

scenario.interaction: a planar cut of limited depth through Example.cut; two right-drags through the mouse handlers of the screen pick tool (through its callbacks where there is no window)
